items.q: What's the difference between an idea and a concept?
items.a: "An idea can be a bit flaky… a **concept is an actual physical thing**." Lock **name, trademark, purpose/why**, and all handles/URLs before going public. Squibb iterated "What's Your Dream" → **Give Without Take** after market feedback.

items.q: Should beginners start cheap or premium?
items.a: **Premium-first pricing** (Apple/Tesla model): start high-end, discount later — hard to go up-market from cheap. Festival shoppers said £50–55 until quality + mission + try-on made **£85** acceptable; display (wooden hangers vs piled hoodies) changes perceived value.

items.q: How do you source inventory with little capital?
items.a: List exact specs; ask everywhere (LinkedIn, coffee shop); negotiate. If broke, ask suppliers to **finance inventory or take equity**. Budget anchor: ~**$4,000 for 200 units**; then 200 → 400 → 800 — don't over-order before product-market fit.

items.q: When is a product "ready" to launch?
items.a: Ship at **80%**, not 100%. "Ship something that's 80% good is better than never shipping it at all." Airbnb launched its website **8 times** before it worked — launch is iterative, not one-shot.

items.q: When should you build warehouses and logistics?
items.a: **Demand before infrastructure**: Royal Mail + personal notes + 3-day supplier reorder beat trucks/warehouses until scale is proven. Even multi-millionaires shouldn't build warehouses before demand.

Early paid ads are a **bidding war**. Prefer content, mission-aligned influencers (often free / revenue-share), and **strategic partnerships** — "1 + 1 = 11" by tapping partner databases that already hold your demographic (e.g. Tide banking).

items.q: Why are influencers and affiliates underpriced?
items.a: "Influencer marketing is the **most underpriced attention** in the market today." Founders will "give the money to Mark Zuckerberg" but won't give profit to their **community affiliates** — reverse that.

items.q: How is a sales system different from marketing?
items.a: After launch: upsell existing buyers, surveys, referral codes, outbound to founders. Pipeline math example: **30 brands → 6 meetings → 1 sponsor**. Negative feedback from **non-fans** beats praise from your core community.

items.q: What financial rules keep a beginner alive?
items.a: Know **COGS and margin** on the wall; never sell below cost; manage cash-flow delay (make → ship → get paid); services take **50% deposit**. Reinvest all profit for years — "Every time you take money off the table, you're **harming the value** of your business a year from now."
